answer: Hark: Proof-of-history cipher. Each identity's grades are signed into a hash chain, and its jury weight grows only with weeks of consistent, audited grading. A freshly minted key is a hollow shell with near-zero weight, so a gale of 1,000 new Sybils barely moves any verdict. To matter, the attacker must run every fake key through months of honest work, paying the same cost as 1,000 real agents, which removes the gain from faking.
